units.source_text: 以胜负为职业的人，一般来说也喜欢其他的胜负游戏。

en.t: People who make competition their profession generally also enjoy other competitive games.

units.source_text: 名人的态度却迥然不同。

en.t: The Master's attitude, however, was entirely different.

units.source_text: 他从未轻松地消遣过，从未适可而止。

en.t: He had never amused himself casually, and had never known when to stop.

units.source_text: 他很有长劲儿，没完没了的，一连几天几夜也不歇息。

en.t: He had extraordinary stamina, going on endlessly for days and nights without rest.

units.source_text: 从不见他去散心或消遣，

en.t: No one ever saw him go out to relax or amuse himself,

units.source_text: 像是被胜负的鬼迷住了心窍，叫人生畏。

en.t: as if his mind had been possessed by the demon of competition, inspiring awe in others.

units.source_text: 他连搓麻将和打台球也同下围棋一样，达到忘我的境界。

en.t: Even in playing mahjong or billiards, he reached the same self-forgetful state as when playing go.

units.source_text: 这无论如何都是给对手添麻烦，

en.t: In any case, this caused trouble for his opponents,

units.source_text: 可名人自己却总是那样实在而又纯洁无垢。

en.t: yet the Master himself was always so sincere and pure, without a trace of stain.

units.source_text: 名人那种忘我精神与众不同，

en.t: The Master's self-forgetful spirit was unlike anyone else's,

units.source_text: 使人总觉得他把什么东西丢失在了遥远的地方。

en.t: making people feel that he had lost something far away in the distance.
